Noncoprime g=gcd(m,k)>1: choose n=(m/g)j with g not dividing j; m not divide n yet m divides kn, so infinitely many orthogonal columns have norms approaching (mk)^((1-alpha)/2)>0, obstructing compactness. For coprime degrees the sparse difference maps e_mj to Delta_j e_kj and vanishes elsewhere, with Delta_j=w_mkj/sqrt(w_mj w_kj)-sqrt(w_mj w_kj)/w_j. Gamma ratio expansion w_n=Gamma(alpha+2)n^(1-alpha)(1-alpha(alpha+1)/(2n)+O(n^-2)) yields Delta_j=-[alpha(alpha+1)/2](m-1)(k-1)/(mk)*(mk)^((1-alpha)/2)/j+O(j^-2). Orthogonality implies the singular multiset is |Delta_j|; rearrangement gives s_n~Lambda/n and summable perturbation of harmonic series gives log partial sums Lambda log N+O(1), Schatten p>1, normalized Dixmier trace Lambda. For alpha=0, w_n=n and coprime Delta=0 exactly. I independently computed Delta_j with exact rational w_n=2n/(n+1) at alpha=1,m=2,k=3 for j=10,100,1000,10000; j Delta_j tends to -1/3 as claimed.
